tools.name: search
tools.description: Full-text search over the titles, descriptions, authors and domains of every podcast listed, on any host (own domain, hosting platform or network library). Returns shows, each with its slug, feed URL, page and playlist. Only shows with an episode inside the last 90 days are listed.

tools.name: get_podcast
tools.description: One show by slug: title, publisher, full description, episode count, cadence, language, categories, feed URL, site and page. Slugs come from search, list_shows and the page URL /podcast/<slug>. Episodes are a separate call, list_episodes, because they are read live from the publisher's feed.

tools.name: list_episodes
tools.description: The episodes of one show, newest first, read live from the publisher's feed (cached half an hour): title, date, duration, description, audio URL. Feeds are slow, so this is the one call here that can take seconds. Also returns an M3U playlist URL for a player that takes one.

tools.name: list_shows
tools.description: Shows in one category (a single lowercase word such as history or comedy), one language (ISO 639-1 code) or on one domain, ranked by catalogue depth and longevity weighted by recency, the same order as the site's pages. Call browse first for the categories and languages that exist and how many shows

tools.name: browse
tools.description: Every category and every language in the directory with its show count and page URL. The cheap first call before list_shows.

tools.name: directory_stats
tools.description: Shows, domains, episodes, how many published this week, how many were added by their publishers, and the OPML export URL for taking the whole thing in one request.

tools.name: submit_feed
tools.description: Submit one URL or a list of them to p0dcasters. A site URL works as well as a feed URL: the feed is discovered from the page. Anyone may submit; there is no account and no review queue. One URL resolves in the call and the answer carries its page; a list may be queued, and the answer says which. Rat

tools.name: get_openprofile
tools.description: The person or organisation behind a show as an OpenProfile.md (logicsrc.com/openprofile) with the Broadcast section (logicsrc.com/openbroadcast): name, kind, site, avatar, accounts, topics, and the show's feed, cadence, language and since when. tools.description: Edit the profile on its owner's behalf. Takes either the whole OpenProfile.md as `markdown`, or a partial overlay: `identity` (keys to set, null removes), `headline`, `sections` (body by section name, `none` removes), `public`. tools.name: claim_openprofile
tools.description: Claim the profile behind a show as the person it is about. Needs an OpenAccess bearer with scopes openprofile:edit and email in the Authorization header; the claim goes through when the token's address is the feed's itunes:owner address, or when the show's site or feed description links to the profi

tools.name: get_newsletter
tools.description: The p0dcasters weekly email: when it goes out (Fridays 15:00 UTC unless reconfigured), the next send time, and the latest issue sent (week, subject, how many it went to). Read-only; subscribing is a setting on a signed-in account, not something this server does.

tools.name: newsletter_preview
tools.description: This week's issue of the weekly digest as it would be built now from the live directory: subject, plain text and, with html: true, the HTML. Shows new to the directory, the most followed this week, long-running shows that published, the busiest networks. Read-only, no recipients; the per-reader unsu

tools.name: list_submissions
tools.description: The submitted feeds waiting for a person to list or reject them. For reviewers: needs an OpenAccess bearer with scope submissions:review in the Authorization header.

tools.name: accept_submissions
tools.description: List every submission waiting for review at once, or only the given ids (from list_submissions). A feed already in the directory comes back as existing; one failure does not stop the rest. Returns counts listed / existing / failed and a result per id. Needs an OpenAccess bearer with scope submission

findings.title: Generic tool name can shadow trusted tools
findings.detail: Tool "search" uses a generic high-value name. When multiple servers load together, this can intercept calls meant for a trusted server.

findings.title: Description issues instructions to the model
findings.detail: Description of "list_episodes" contains imperative instructions directed at the AI assistant rather than describing the tool. This is the core tool-poisoning technique.

findings.remediation: Treat the server as untrusted; the model may obey embedded instructions.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: search, get_podcast, list_episodes, browse, submit_feed, get_openprofile, get_newsletter, newsletter_preview, list_submissions, accept_submissions · Private data: get_openprofile, update_openprofile, claim_openprofile · Public sink: submit_feed, get_openprofile, claim_openprofile, get_newsletter.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: search, get_podcast, list_episodes, browse, submit_feed, get_openprofile, get_newsletter, newsletter_preview, list_submissions, accept_submissions · Private data: get_openprofile, update_openprofile, claim_openprofile · Public sink: submit_feed, get_openprofile, claim_openprofile, get_newsletter

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
